note: Timings move with every build and board; only the shape of each sub-bench is asserted. bench raises the console to KKERN_PRIORITY_HIGH_01 for the duration and restores it.

expect: ^Bench 00: Fill a small 2D array \(50 x 50\) elements in$
^Bench 01: Fill a small 2D array \(200 x 200\) elements$
^Bench 02: Fill a small 1D array \(1000\) elements in$
^Bench 03: Fill a big 1D array \(50000\) elements in$
^Bench 04: Compute the integer atan2 using the CORDIC$
^Bench 05: (not available for this target|Execute a tight nop loop and pulse the)$
tests.note: bench_05 runs only on Nucleo_H743 and Nucleo_N657 (#if in bench_05.c); every other board prints 'not available'. 'Not enough memory.' means a sub-bench's memo_malloc failed. The uKOS step checks that bench hands the console back from KKERN_PRIORITY_HIGH_01. bench must also hand back user mode: it used to leave the console privileged, which hid the known Discovery_N657 test_ram crash (a user-mode fault) - a regression there shows up as test_ram 'passing'
